**Fixes from a review of the whole code base.** A folder can no longer be
moved into itself, files over 256 GiB are refused clearly, and a few rare
cases that could keep a drive from opening, or slow it down, are fixed.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.6.7-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.6.7-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## Fixed

- **Moving a folder into one of its own subfolders** with the `cloak`
  command line could leave a drive that wouldn't open. It's now refused.
  (On a mounted drive, Windows already refused it.)
- **Files over 256 GiB** made the drive fail with a confusing error part-way
  through a copy. A file in a drive can be at most 256 GiB, and now a
  larger one is refused straight away with a clear message. Converting a
  folder lists any such files before it starts.
- **A crash while the drive saved its list of missing items** could make the
  next unlock re-lock every file in the drive, which takes a while on a big
  drive. That no longer happens.
- **A drive whose top folder held files from many other drives** could say
  "wrong password" to its own password. It now opens.

## Known limitations

- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
- Hidden files of the same drive can be shown to belong together (they share
  the lock's salt); a file on its own looks random.
